# US-005 — Schema tests, conformance checks, command-reference docs, and version bump

**Story ID:** US-005  
**Priority:** P1  
**Tasks:** T-005  
**Status:** Shipped (QA PASS)

## Who uses this and why

A planr contributor who modifies any part of the dashboard codebase in the future.
This story ensures that changes that break the schema, introduce off-palette hex
values, use forbidden brand codenames, or regress existing behaviour will be
caught automatically by `npm test` and the conformance check before they merge.
It also ensures the command is discoverable and understandable: `docs/dashboard.md`
explains the command to new users.

## What it does

### Test suite (`tests/dashboard/`, `tests/schema/`)

Four test files cover the dashboard end-to-end:

- **`tests/schema/graph-schema.test.mjs`** — validates `schemas/v1.0.0/graph.schema.json`
  against known-valid and known-invalid Graph fixtures. 5 subtests. (Note: the QA
  report lists 39 schema tests total, which includes pre-existing schema tests plus
  this file.)
- **`tests/dashboard/graph-equivalence.test.mjs`** — asserts that the native
  reader and the CLI delegate produce equivalent graphs for the shared fixture
  project in `conformance/fixtures/dashboard-graph/`. 3 subtests.
- **`tests/dashboard/server.test.mjs`** — verifies the server starts on a free
  port, responds to `GET /api/graph` with a valid Graph, serves `GET /api/events`
  as `text/event-stream`, and reuses a running instance instead of spawning a
  second one. 5 subtests total across the dashboard test files.
- **`tests/dashboard/watcher.test.mjs`** — asserts the debounce window (writes
  within 300ms collapse to one event) and the incremental-recompute scope (only
  the changed node's subgraph is recomputed).

All 139 tests across the full test suite pass (`npm test` exit 0) with zero
regressions to pre-existing orchestration, design, and design-engine test suites.

### Conformance check (`conformance/verify-dashboard.mjs`)

`verify-dashboard.mjs` is a self-contained Node-ESM script that runs three checks
and exits non-zero on any failure:

1. **Palette fidelity.** Scans all text files under `lib/dashboard/` (excluding
   `lib/dashboard/vendor/` — attributed third-party runtime) and `docs/dashboard.md`
   for hex color literals. Compares each against the 30 tokens in
   `.planr/design-system/tokens.css`. Any off-palette hex is a failure.
2. **Brand hygiene.** Checks the same file set for third-party product codenames
   (denylist is fragment-assembled so the check never spells the forbidden names).
3. **Schema presence.** Confirms `schemas/v1.0.0/graph.schema.json` exists and
   parses as JSON.

The script exits 0 on all checks passing, which is confirmed by `node conformance/verify-dashboard.mjs` in CI (QA: exit 0).

### Command-reference documentation (`docs/dashboard.md`)

`docs/dashboard.md` is the user-facing reference for the `/planr-pipeline:dashboard`
command. It covers: synopsis, flag reference, how it works (mode resolution, graph
sourcing, server lifetime, URL printout), relationship to `/planr-pipeline:status`,
the read-only guarantee, the empty state, live sync, and export. It does not
duplicate the agent-facing step sequence — that lives in `commands/dashboard.md`.
See [`docs/dashboard.md`](../../docs/dashboard.md) — this file should be the
canonical reference; do not duplicate it here.

### Version bump and CHANGELOG

`package.json` version was bumped from 0.20.0 → 0.21.0. `CHANGELOG.md` received
a new `[0.21.0] 2026-06-14` entry describing the dashboard feature, matching the
format of existing changelog entries.
